newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Selected quotes from Russia-China declaration.
newsitem.headline: Selected quotes from Russia-China declaration.

text.p: The following are excerpts from the Russian-Chinese declaration signed on Wednesday by Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Chinese President Jiang Zemin.
The quotes from the "Russian-Chinese Joint Declaration on the Multi-Polar World and Forming a New World Order" were translated by Reuters from a Russian text distributed by the Kremlin.

-- On Military Blocs: "Both sides express concern over the attempt at enlarging and strengthening military blocs because such a tendency may pose a threat to the security of some countries and aggravate regional and global tension."

-- The Current International Situation: "The two sides consider that international relations at the end of the 20th century have undergone profound changes. The Cold War has ended. The bi-polar system has ceased to exist. The positive trend towards a multi-polar world is accelerating."

"A growing number of countries are coming to the understanding that they need mutual respect, equality and mutual benefit rather than hegemonism and power politics, dialogue and cooperation rather than confrontation and conflicts."

-- On the New World Order: "All countries, big or small, strong or weak, rich or poor, are equal members of the international community. No country should seek hegemony, practice power politics or monopolise international affairs."
"Both sides believe that the Cold War mentality should be abandoned and they oppose the policy of (military) blocs"

-- On Disarmament: "The two sides are committed to promoting the process of disarmament. They stress the importance of the signing of the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty and the implementation of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty."

On the United Nations: "The U.N. should focus its peacekeeping efforts on the prevention and spread of conflicts. Peacekeeping operations can be undertaken only by the decision of the U.N. Security Council and the approval of the countries concerned, and in strict compliance with the Security Council mandate and its supervision."

"When deciding to impose sanctions in accordance with relevant provisions of the U.N. Charter, the Security Council should see to it that the losses caused by the measure as well as the losses it brings to third countries and adjacent areas be reduced to the minimum. Sanctions should be lessened or removed in due course in the process of the implementation of the Security Council resolutions."
-- On the Third World: "The rise (of the developing world) will give a strong boost to the historical process towards the establishment of a new international order."
"They (developing countries) should take a rightful place in the future new international order, participating, on an equal basis, in international affairs free from any discrimination."
